dedupe_keys.name: platform for economic analysis of climate hazards peach gridded hazards and exposure 2000 2019

description: PEACH is a quasi-global gridded database of hazard and socioeconomic exposure, with monthly values on a grid of about 10 by 10 km from 2000 to 2019 and full coverage from 2004 to 2015. It covers 14 climate impact drivers (mean temperature, cold spells, extreme heat, mean and heavy precipitation, river and pluvial floods, landslides, drought, fire weather and wildfires, severe windstorms, tropical cyclones, sand and dust, hail, and air pollution) and three geophysical hazards (earthquakes, volcanic eruptions and tsunamis), plus six exposure variables including population, night lights, relative wealth, critical infrastructure, vegetation and land use. Unlike event lists it avoids fixed inclusion thresholds, so users can define extremes themselves. It was built by Robert Reinhardt of the Centre d'Économie de la Sorbonne and described in a 2025 working paper; version 2.0 (October 2025) is on Zenodo in Apache Arrow Feather files by UN M49 subregion, with R and Python loading scripts, under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, with access on request for non-commercial research. Caveats: rainfall is limited to 50 N to 50 S, dust is a proxy, and access is restricted. It supports hazard exposure panels for economic impact and infrastructure risk studies; a related record is EM-DAT.
name: Platform for Economic Analysis of Climate Hazards (PEACH) gridded hazards and exposure 2000-2019
provider: Robert Reinhardt, Centre d'Économie de la Sorbonne (Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne)
